text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The National Oil Company proposed a rise in the price of petrol to 1,700 lei per litre possibly starting in January.

- International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus is expected in Bucharest this evening. He will meet Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu and members of parliament.

- Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said the telephone company Rom Telecom RA will turn into a shareholding company with the state as the majority stockholder. A minority stake will be sold to a strategic investor only after the company has grown financially stable, he said.
- The Transport Ministry plans to increase train fares to cut losses.
- Tarom SA airline plans to buy seven ATR planes next year. The cost of one aircraft is $13 million.
- It will take 10 years to restructure the national railway company SNCFR, Transport Minister Traian Basescu says in an interview.
ADEVARUL
- Fertiliser maker Azomures SA, which dominates trading on the Bucharest stock exchange, is vital for the bourse's activity.

- Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd, currently the largest single investor in Romania, plans to put another $473 million into its joint venture with a Romanian carmaker next year, when the output target is more than 100,000 cars.
AZI
- Romanian oil exploration company Petrom RA plans to bid for concessions of oil blocs in northern Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
LIBERTATEA
- The limit on Romania's indebtness next year is $3.0 billion.
General:
ADEVARUL
- President Emil Constantinescu will meet NATO chief Javier Solana during a visit to NATO headquarters in Brussels on February 4.
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on the fate of the members of former dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's family.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), defeated in last month's parliamentary elections, is expected to undergo radical changes during its national conference scheduled for January 10.
- Foreign Minister Adrian Severin wants ambassadorial posts to be subject to tests.
- The economic Crans-Montana forum will be held in Romania next year, said forum chairman Jean-Paul Carteron.

- The Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR) accuses Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's government of having created the conditions for autonomy on ethnic grounds by including the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) in the coalition cabinet.
DIMINEATA

- "The Romanian Revolution from December 1989 entered history accompanied by the name of the man who gave it senss and identity -- Ion Iliescu," reads a front-page headline on a report on the events seven years ago.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The European Parliament issued a resolution calling for protection of children living in the streets of Romania's major towns.
LIBERTATEA
- A Romanian boy living in Bucharest's streets tells his story about his life with a French paedophile.
ZIUA
- Leaders of associations of December 1989 revolutionaries want all criminal cases involving journalists to be dropped. ($=3,912 lei) -- Bucharest newsroom 40-3120264
